item.title: Little-Parks Oscillations and Parity Effects in Mesoscopic Superconducting Rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.14597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analytically investigate the Little-Parks (LP) effect, the periodic oscillation of the superconducting transition temperature $T_c$ driven by an applied magnetic flux $\Phi$, from the weak-coupling Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) limit to the intermediate-coupling regime in a mesoscopic, quasi-one-dimensional ring. Utilizing a Ginzburg-Landau (GL) expansion with twisted boundary conditions, we correctly incorporate both the discrete finite-size topological parity interference and the continuous center-of-mass (CM) kinetic energy shift induced by the supercurrent. We derive a closed-form expression for $T_c(\Phi)$ valid within the GL framework across variable interaction strengths. We demonstrate that the LP response comprises two distinct physical contributions: a discrete topological parity effect governed by the correlation length ratio $\xi/R$, and a continuous kinetic energy term scaling as $1/R^2$. As the coupling increases and the spatial correlation length of the pairs contracts ($\xi \ll R$), the constituent pairs become geometrically blind to the global boundary constraint, leading to an exponential suppression of the discrete parity modulation. However, the requirement that the condensate acquires a flux-dependent macroscopic CM momentum persists. This ensures that the critical temperature $T_c$ maintains an algebraic LP modulation driven predominantly by the macroscopic kinetic energy of the supercurrent. We bound our theoretical approach by discussing the breakdown of mean-field GL validity before phase fluctuations dominate near the strong-coupling limit.
item.dc:creator: Iogann Tolbatov, Luca Salasnich

item.title: Symmetry-Enabled Rolling of Composite Bosons: A Route to Superconductivity from Strong Repulsion with $T_c$ Proportional to the Electron Bandwidth
item.description: arXiv:2611.14615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by superconductors discovered in systems with a strong Coulomb repulsion, we ask whether such a repulsion can give rise to superconductivity with a transition temperature $T_c$ bounded only by the electron bandwidth. Coulomb repulsion can produce pairing as it binds electrons to holes. If each hole binds three electrons into a three-electron-one-hole (3e1h) composite, the condensation of these bosonic composites can give rise to superconductivity. However, the resulting $T_c$ falls far below the electron bandwidth in the controlled regime where the binding is much stronger than the carriers' kinetic energy. This is because, on a lattice, a tightly bound composite usually has to move through a higher-order process where the intermediate state costs an energy of order the binding energy, so that the strong binding makes the composite heavy, limiting the superfluid stiffness and hence $T_c$. Here, we show that symmetry offers a way around this tradeoff. In lattices satisfying certain symmetry requirements, a composite can move by single-particle hops without any costly intermediate state, a motion we call rolling. Such rolling keeps the mass of the composite finite even for an infinitely strong binding, so that a $T_c$ proportional to the electron bandwidth can be achieved in the controlled regime. We derive a criterion for rolling and apply it to construct all fourteen minimal lattice models that support such rolling. We show that rollable 3e1h composites can indeed be stabilized in the ground state. We then propose to realize such superconductivity in a dual-gate bilayer, and use exact numerics to show that $T_c$ can reach a few percent of the electron hopping. These results establish rollability as a guiding principle in the search for and design of superconductors in strongly repelling electron systems, with the minimal models constructed here as prototypes.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyu Dong

item.title: Nitride crystalline barrier epitaxial SIS Josephson junctions by MBE
item.description: arXiv:2611.14968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconductor-insulator-superconductor Josephson junctions with crystalline tunnel barriers have remained elusive by epitaxial techniques such as MOCVD or MBE that produce the junction materials and devices powering today's electronic and photonic systems like transistors and lasers. Here, we overcome the key materials hurdle to realize the first functional nitride crystalline barrier Josephson junctions by MBE. Despite an AlN barrier thickness of approximately 4.5 nm, the NbN/AlN/NbN trilayers exhibit coherent Josephson tunneling with critical current densities of approximately 17 A/cm2, an IcRn product of approximately 2.5 mV, and a superconducting gap voltage of approximately 3.7 mV with a BCS-like gap evolution with temperature. Hysteretic current-voltage characteristics and Fraunhofer current modulation with magnetic field establish underdamped SIS Josephson behavior. The realization of crystalline barrier Josephson junctions by MBE opens the doors to a richer materials palette with alloys and superlattice electrodes and tunnel barriers, as well as potential monolithic integration of superconducting quantum circuits with active electronic and photonic devices such as HEMTs and lasers.

item.title: Interplay of Pair Density Wave and Uniform Superconductivity on the Kagome Lattice
item.description: arXiv:2611.15354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the interplay between pair density wave (PDW) and uniform superconductivity on the kagome lattice within a single-orbital $t$-$W$-$J$ model near the $p$-type van Hove filling, where $W$ and $J$ denote effective pairing attractions on lattice sites and nearest-neighbor bonds, respectively. While onsite attraction favors zero-momentum pairing through the conventional BCS instability, nearest-neighbor attraction naturally promotes finite-momentum pairing due to the kagome geometry and sublattice interference. The model therefore provides a framework for exploring the competition and coexistence between uniform superconductivity and PDW order. Self-consistent mean-field calculations in a $2\times2$ supercell reveal that the uniform component reorganizes both the amplitudes and phase structure of the three $F_1$ PDW components, giving rise to superconducting states absent in the pure bond-pairing limit. A Ginzburg--Landau analysis identifies symmetry-allowed couplings that can favor this reorganization. The resulting states exhibit distinct charge modulations and quasiparticle spectra, while the chiral PDW undergoes topological transitions as the onsite attraction increases. Our results demonstrate how uniform superconductivity reshapes the order-parameter landscape and quasiparticle topology of a PDW state.
item.dc:creator: Ruiqing Fu, Xianxin Wu, Ziqiang Wang, Sen Zhou

item.title: Machine-accelerated extraction of experimental superconducting parameters for physical insight and prediction across thousands of materials
item.description: arXiv:2611.15627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: New superconductors could unlock next-generation technologies from nuclear fusion to lossless electronics. Machine learning can predict candidate superconductors but lacks validated experimental training data beyond the critical temperature. Here we present AutoSuperCon, a database of eight superconducting parameters, containing 20354 entries for 6793 superconductors. The data were extracted from over 47000 arXiv preprints using a large language model and validated against reference datasets ($R^2 = 0.96$ with NIMS SuperCon). Using AutoSuperCon, we show that median gap ratios rise from 3.6 in conventional superconductors to 6.4 in cuprates, 28% of upper critical fields exceed the Pauli limit, and critical temperatures lie below a ceiling proportional to the superfluid density. Further, we train composition-based predictors for the critical temperature ($R^2_{\log}=0.83$) and the upper critical field ($R^2_{\log}=0.69$), boosted by transfer learning. Within known superconducting families, composition alone is sufficient to screen candidates for both parameters. AutoSuperCon thus enables physical insight and data-driven discovery across thousands of superconductors.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Manium, Benjamin Geisler, Peter J. Hirschfeld, Amalia I. Coldea

item.title: Band geometry, Anderson's theorem, and vortex nucleation in unconventional 2D superconductors
item.description: arXiv:2611.15872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the recent discovery of chiral superconductors in 2d materials, we study the effects of disorder on superconductivity in materials with non-trivial band geometry. First, we show how Anderson's theorem and the conventional Abrikosov-Gorkov description of disorder-induced pair breaking are modified by the structure of the normal-state Bloch functions. We apply these results to twisted MoTe2 and show that a BCS pairing mechanism for the observed superconductor is in tension with the measured normal state residual resistivity. Second, we study whether random potential disorder can nucleate superconducting vortices in a chiral time- reversal-breaking superconductor. We show that, for a superconductor stabilized by the usual BCS mechanism, weak disorder does not induce a vortex glass phase, in contrast to superconductivity formed from an anyon fluid.
item.dc:creator: Vladislav Poliakov, Inti Sodemann Villadiego, T. Senthil

item.title: Evidence of anisotropic surface state residual loss in UTe$_2$ amid isotropic low-energy excitations
item.description: arXiv:2611.16196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore the pairing mechanism and possible topological properties of the unconventional superconductor UTe$_2$ through their influence on both the inductive and resistive channels using resonant cavity perturbation techniques. We measure a composite surface impedance for a variety of UTe$_2$ single crystals at microwave frequencies, where the inductive and resistive channels are comparable and can be treated on equal footing. By studying the composite electrodynamics for a large number of resonant modes, we are able to provide a comprehensive picture of the directional dependence of the excitations out of the ground state. We find similar power-law temperature dependencies at low-temperature for both the penetration depth and surface resistance, which in aggregate across modes, are quadratic and isotropic. On the other hand, we find a distinct and systematic anisotropy of the residual loss. The power-law results are inconsistent with a single pair of point nodes on the Fermi surface under weak scattering. We discuss the possibility of topological superconductivity as an interpretation of these isotropic power-laws in conjunction with the anisotropic residual loss.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Carlton-Jones, Jared Z. Dans, Gicela Saucedo Salas, Shanta R. Saha, Johnpierre Paglione, Nicholas P. Butch, Steven M. Anlage

item.title: Quantum geometry drives orbital paramagnetism in superconducting fluctuations
item.description: arXiv:2611.16387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconductors expel magnetic fields through the Meissner effect. Even slightly above the superconducting transition temperature, electrons can briefly form Cooper pairs, leading to an orbital diamagnetic susceptibility that diverges as the transition is approached. In this work, we use Gaussian fluctuation theory to study a generic multicomponent superconductor above its transition temperature and show that fluctuations can instead produce a paramagnetic response. We identify two competing contributions: the usual diamagnetic contribution from the center-of-mass motion of Cooper pairs and a paramagnetic contribution from interference between different components of the superconducting order parameter. The latter is related to pair quantum geometry, which describes how the internal components of the Cooper pair change with momentum. We then apply our theory to a model of a kagome superconductor with two chiral pairing modes. When the parent state preserves time-reversal symmetry, the paramagnetic contribution can outweigh the conventional diamagnetic contribution, producing net fluctuation paramagnetism. However, when the orbital time-reversal symmetry is broken, e.g., by forming a weak loop-current order, the degeneracy between the two chiral modes is then lifted. Upon cooling toward the superconducting transition, the lower-energy mode dominates the fluctuations, and diamagnetism wins as single-component physics takes over. Our results provide a mechanism for fluctuation paramagnetism in superconductors and show that the orbital magnetic response can probe the quantum geometry of Cooper pairs.
item.dc:creator: Zi-Ting Sun, Ying-Ming Xie, Chunli Huang, Naoto Nagaosa

item.title: Noise-Protected Superconducting Qudits from Higher-Harmonic Josephson Junctions
item.description: arXiv:2611.16563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Qudits, which generalize qubits to $d$ levels, store more information per circuit element than qubits. As with qubits, however, their sensitivity to noise must be overcome before they can be used for fault-tolerant quantum computing. Here we show that, by exploiting the second harmonic of the current--phase relation, a superconducting loop of three Josephson junctions can host qutrits strongly protected against relaxation, while dephasing limits their coherence. When the second harmonic is positive, a simple loop with a small asymmetry between the junctions provides a tunable, symmetry-protected qutrit. When it is negative, a protected qutrit can be realized by adding a small symmetry-breaking term, such as a weak Josephson diode effect. The two designs involve different trade-offs: the first has an exact charge selection rule, whereas the second is nearly insensitive to charge noise and its quasiparticle errors can be corrected. The preferable choice therefore depends on the materials used. Both require a sizable second harmonic to begin with, and we identify altermagnetic Josephson junctions as a candidate platform. Finally, microscopic calculations show that a gate voltage selects the sign of the second harmonic in these junctions, although gate-voltage noise then becomes the leading source of dephasing. These findings establish the sign of the second harmonic as a design principle for protected superconducting qudits.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Vakili

item.title: Sign changing pairing in single layer FeSe/SrTiO3 revealed by nonmagnetic impurity bound states
item.description: arXiv:2611.16679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in single layer FeSe epitaxially grown on SrTiO3(001) substrates has instigated extensive debate over whether its pairing symmetry is conventional sign-preserving s-wave or unconventional sign-changing. Here we probe the pairing state for single layer FeSe/SrTiO3 grown by molecular beam epitaxy using scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy. We observe robust in-gap bound states induced by non-magnetic Fe-vacancy defects within the Fe-plane, which exhibit strong spatial electron-hole asymmetry with two-fold symmetry in hole states and four-fold in electron states. The bound states exhibit no energy shift or splitting under an applied magnetic field, consistent with a sign-changing order parameter.
item.dc:creator: Huimin Zhang, Zhuozhi Ge, Michael Weinert, Lian Li

item.title: Singlet-triplet superconductivity from repulsive interactions in a $p$-wave magnet
item.description: arXiv:2611.14609v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by recent proposals of $p$-wave magnets, which host odd-parity spin splitting, we study electrons near Van Hove singularities with local repulsive interactions. We demonstrate how the symmetry of the $p$-wave spin splitting governs the competition among instabilities. Using a parquet renormalization group (pRG) analysis of a simple one-sublattice model of a $p$-wave magnet, we find that superconductivity is the leading instability over the entire phase diagram for purely repulsive interactions. The resulting superconducting state is generically a mixture of spin-singlet and spin-triplet pairing and approaches an equal-weight mixture when $T_c$ is small compared with the energy offset between each Van Hove electron and its inversion partner. Extending the pRG analysis to a more realistic two-sublattice model, we find that superconductivity remains the leading instability, while the sublattice degree of freedom leads to a competition among various singlet-triplet pairing channels and even a finite-momentum equal-spin pair-density wave. Our mechanism applies broadly to odd-parity magnets and opens a natural route to nodal topological superconductivity.
item.dc:creator: Hanbit Oh, Laura Classen, Daniel F. Agterberg

item.title: Squeezed Light Generation by Cooper Pair Recombination in a Superconductor-Semiconductor Structure
item.description: arXiv:2611.14622v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We theoretically demonstrate squeezed light generation in a compact, electrically driven device utilizing the nonlinear light-matter interaction of Cooper-pair recombination in a hybrid superconductorsemiconductor structure. On the basis of second-order perturbation theory, we developed an effective Hamiltonian which incorporates the electronic component of the interaction as a photon coupling strength coefficient, enabling a model to describe the quadrature squeezing effect of Cooper-pair recombination on the photonic state. We find the squeezing strength to be proportional to the superconducting energy gap squared and device length, as well as increasing with applied voltage. For practical device length, materials and voltage bias, we calculated squeezing values comparable to those of existing squeezed light generation methods when operating below the critical temperature. This theoretically developed concept shows viability for electrically pumped squeezed light generation and can pave the way towards realization of squeezing in compact integrated structures.
item.dc:creator: Sima Buchbinder, Avi Koriat, Alex Hayat

item.title: Interplay of the Fano-Andreev Effect and Nonlinear Screening in Electric and Thermoelectric Transport through a T-Shaped Double Quantum Dot
item.description: arXiv:2611.14991v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a theoretical study of weakly nonlinear electric and thermoelectric transport through a T-shaped double quantum dot coupled to normal and superconducting leads. Nonlinear screening is treated within the characteristic-potential formalism, in which an internal electrostatic potential accounts for nonequilibrium charge redistribution on the lead-coupled central dot. The side-coupled dot induces the Fano-Andreev effect, which, together with nonlinear screening, significantly modifies the transport properties. Under voltage bias, the screening-induced level renormalization produces a pronounced bias asymmetry in the Andreev differential conductance. In response to a pure thermal bias, increasing the interdot coupling weakens the level renormalization and suppresses the quasiparticle thermoelectric response, leading to reduced thermovoltage and nonlinear Seebeck coefficient. When voltage and thermal biases are applied simultaneously, a finite subgap cross thermoelectric response emerges beyond the linear regime. The sign of this response is governed by the competition between the energy-dependent transport contribution, modified by the Fano-Andreev effect, and the nonlinear screening contribution, thereby determining whether a thermal bias enhances or suppresses the low-bias Andreev current.
item.dc:creator: Sachin Verma

item.title: Reducing TLS Losses in Superconducting Circuits Using Solid Neon
item.description: arXiv:2611.15021v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Two level systems (TLSs) are a major source of loss in superconducting devices, limiting the performance of qubits, detectors, and resonators. These defects arise from a range of sources, including surface oxides, crystal defects, as well as fabrication residues which are often difficult to remove. Using NbTiN coplanar waveguide resonators, we show that depositing and subsequently removing a solid neon film can significantly improve device performance. Analysis of the temperature and power dependence indicates that this enhancement arises from reduced TLS dissipation, which we attribute to the redistribution and removal of surface contaminants during neon deposition and evaporation. Atomic force microscopy images of contaminated hexagonal boron nitride flakes before and after neon exposure show that neon treatment can redistribute and remove surface residues. These results demonstrate a simple, non-destructive approach for mitigating TLS losses in superconducting devices and other sensitive materials that cannot withstand aggressive cleaning processes.
item.dc:creator: A. Palmer, K. Matkovic, P. Russell, E. Helgemo, L. Delventhal, Y. Ashlea Alava, K. Zuo, S. N. Coppersmith, M. C. Cassidy

item.title: Multifractal collective order : Application to multifractal superconductivity in dodecagonal quasicrystals
item.description: arXiv:2611.15446v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conventional descriptions of collective ordering often assume spatially uniform order parameters, although the underlying electronic states can exhibit strong spatial inhomogeneity or multifractality. Here, we demonstrate that deterministic aperiodic geometry can instead stabilize multifractal collective order. We formulate a general diagnostic applicable to superconducting, magnetic, and charge channels, combining direct scaling analysis of the order parameter with three criteria: its spatial hierarchy must be dictated by the underlying geometry, emerge in the leading ordering instability, and persist in the self-consistent ordered state below a single mean-field ordering onset. We demonstrate that superconductivity on the experimentally resolved Ti network of a dodecagonal oxide quasicrystal satisfies all three criteria. The resulting condensate exhibits multifractal scaling over the resolved range of spatial scales, retaining its hierarchical structure throughout the ordered phase and channeling flux-induced equilibrium currents along geometry-locked rings.
item.dc:creator: SeHyun Park, Junmo Jeon, SungBin Lee

item.title: Mapping the High-Field Response of Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detectors
item.description: arXiv:2611.16071v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) are increasingly being integrated into cryogenic quantum-sensing platforms that operate in large magnetic fields. Here, the high-field limits of these measurements were probed by characterizing the dark count response of a NbTiN SNSPD at up to 14~T using in situ control of the detector orientation and benchmarking that performance against normal detector operation in smaller magnetic fields. The detector performance is strongly anisotropic: perpendicular magnetic fields rapidly reduce the usable bias-current range, whereas near-parallel alignment enables operation at substantially larger total fields, with a finite operating margin retained to 12~T and measurable dark-count response at the 14~T field limit. The angular dependence is governed predominantly by the perpendicular component of the magnetic field, consistent with vortex-mediated suppression of the superconducting current scale. The same field-dependent current scale also determines the electrical pulse amplitude, linking high-field detector operation directly to readout performance. These results establish a practical route for deploying SNSPDs in multi-tesla quantum-sensing and high-field cryogenic experiments.
item.dc:creator: Harshit Agarwal, Yueh-Chun Wu, Katyayani Seal, Niels Noordzij, Andreas Fognini, Ronan Gourgues, G\'abor B. Hal\'asz, Benjamin J. Lawrie, Nirjhar Sarkar

item.title: Why "quantum spin liquids'' are quantum singlet liquids
item.description: arXiv:2611.16428v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The last couple of decades have seen enormous theoretical and experimental research efforts aimed at finding quantum spin liquids (QSLs) in geometrically frustrated (GF) magnetic materials. Experimental demonstrations of QSLs are challenging due to the indirect character of possible QSL signatures and the presence of impurities in materials, which may destroy or obscure a QSL. At the same time, theoretical literature often lacks consensus about the ground states of quantum spins on even the simplest GF magnetic lattices. We summarize experimental evidence that in the impurity-free limit, available GF magnetic materials that do not develop magnetic order at low temperatures would form {\it a quantum singlet liquid}, i.e. a disordered state of non-magnetic excitations. We further confirm the existence of such a singlet liquid and its gapless character with theoretical arguments. Such a liquid manifests itself in the thermodynamics of GF magnets while having no magnetic features at low temperatures.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Syzranov, Arthur P. Ramirez

item.title: Dislocation Arrays Hosting Topological Bound States in Epitaxial Tetragonal FeSe Films
item.description: arXiv:2611.16681v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Topological defects in real space can host robust, localized quantum states for quantum information processing and sensing, yet deterministic control over their formation in crystalline materials remain challenging.
item.dc:creator: Huimin Zhang, Basu Oli, Zhengfei Wang, Michael Weinert, Lian Li

item.title: A superconducting quantum point contact in Ge
item.description: arXiv:2611.16705v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hybrid superconducting-semiconducting circuits provide a versatile platform for investigating coherent transport in mesoscopic weak links. Superconducting quantum point contacts (SQPCs) are particularly interesting in this context, as their supercurrent is carried by a discrete number of ballistic transport modes. Here, we investigate a gate-tunable superconducting quantum point contact realized in Ge/SiGe. By incorporating the QPC into a highly asymmetric superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID), we gain access to its current-phase relation (CPR) and switching current, enabling phase-sensitive studies of few-mode superconducting transport. We observe a direct correspondence between conductance quantization and switching-current quantization, linking the normal-state transport modes to the superconducting response. In addition, we demonstrate strong gate tunability of the effective transmission near the onset of the first conductance plateau. Under microwave irradiation, the QPC exhibits photon-assisted multiple Andreev reflections at lower transparencies and Shapiro replicas in the high-transparency, few-mode regime.
item.dc:creator: Anna Tacchini, Inga Seidler, Isabell Grandt-Ionita, Thibault Thuegaz, Stephen W. Bedell, Fabrizio Nichele

item.title: Symmetry-Controlled Criticality and Zeno Localization in a Monitored Quasiperiodic Superconductor
item.description: arXiv:2611.16912v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Measurement-induced transitions of free fermions depend strongly on symmetry, but their interplay with quasiperiodic localization and superconducting pairing remains largely unexplored. We study a continuously monitored model of free fermions with pairing, where quasiperiodicity both controls localization and changes the symmetry class of the monitored field theory. Using topological entanglement entropy as a probe of nonlocal correlations in quantum state diffusion simulations, we identify a transition between a critical phase whose von Neumann entanglement entropy scales as $(\ln L)^2$ and an area-law phase, whereas no transition occurs in the clean limit, consistent with the corresponding DIII and D nonlinear sigma models. The transition line exhibits strong multifractality and depends nonmonotonically on quasiperiodicity, which we associate with the symmetry crossover. Deep in the Zeno regime, we derive an effective non-Hermitian Bogoliubov-de Gennes description of individual trajectories and obtain a closed-form localization length that quantitatively agrees with numerics. Our results reveal how symmetry, quasiperiodic localization, and measurement backaction combine to determine both critical entanglement and microscopic trajectory localization in monitored superconductors.
item.dc:creator: Pinaki Singha, Marcin Szyniszewski, Nilanjan Roy, Auditya Sharma

item.title: Reflection Zeros Set the Scattering Invariant of Finite Majorana Wires
item.description: arXiv:2611.17001v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Majorana modes, zero-energy excitations of superconducting wires that are their own antiparticles, could store quantum information protected from local noise. In transport experiments, however, ordinary bound states mimic their signature, a conductance peak at zero voltage, and whether Majorana modes have been observed remains debated. A sign, $Q$, of the electron reflection at zero energy marks the topological phase of a long wire, but what $Q$ certifies in a finite device has been unclear. Here we show for the first time that $Q$ counts reflectionless states, waves that enter through one contact and leave entirely through the other: $Q=-1$ when an odd number of them lie in the lower half of the complex energy plane. In a finite wire this means that the two Majorana modes are split by less than their coupling to the contacts. With equal contacts, every sign change of $Q$, including the bulk topological transition, is an exceptional point at which two such states merge and transmission is maximally flat. At zero temperature, $Q=-1$ exactly when the zero-bias conductance measured at a contact exceeds $e^2/h$. These results show what transport can certify about a Majorana device and how to read the invariant from conductance.
item.dc:creator: Alex Krasnok

item.title: Evidence for time-reversal symmetry breaking and glassy dynamics in superconducting (La,Pr,Sm)3Ni2O7 films
item.description: arXiv:2508.16412v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Superconductivity and magnetism are generally distinct and competing orders, characterized by different broken symmetries and order parameters. Although they may coexist in some correlated systems, whether and how these orders can become inherently intertwined in unconventional high-transition-temperature (high-Tc) superconductors remains a central open question. Here, we report time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking and glassy dynamics in the superconducting state of nickelate (La,Pr,Sm)3Ni2O7 films. Magnetoresistance hysteresis and zero-field non-reciprocal charge transport, complementary evidence for broken TRS, are observed in the superconducting state, while absent in the normal state. Within the superconducting transition regime, logarithmically slow resistance relaxations following magnetic-field perturbations provide strong evidence for glassy dynamics. Remarkably, the reproducible temperature hierarchy across multiple films reveals that these novel phenomena emerge concurrently with developing superconducting phase coherence, preceding the zero-resistance state. Consistently, scanning superconducting quantum interference device (sSQUID) microscopy directly resolves the zero-field magnetic-flux patterns indicative of spontaneous TRS breaking, which emerge simultaneously with local superconducting diamagnetism and phase stiffness. Our observations suggest a frustrated multicomponent superconducting order parameter in the nickelate films, whose internal relative phases may carry TRS-breaking chirality and freeze into a textured phase glass. Collectively, our findings identify a distinctive form of superconductivity in which internal phase degrees of freedom may support additional broken symmetries and glassy order, offering a new perspective on intertwined ordering phenomena in unconventional high-Tc superconductors.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Ji, Zheyuan Xie, Yaqi Chen, Guangdi Zhou, Keyi Liang, Rui Liu, Mengqiao Geng, Meixuan Li, Longxin Pan, Heng Wang, Haoliang Huang, Jun Ge, Yi Liu, Yang Liu, Guang-Ming Zhang, Yihua Wang, Ziqiang Wang, Qi-Kun Xue, Zhuoyu Chen, Jian Wang

item.title: Emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi Surfaces in hybrid Al/InAs heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2608.06553v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the microwave electrodynamics of a proximitized two-dimensional electron gas in hybrid superconductor/semiconductor heterostructures. Using lumped-element resonators with inductor wires oriented relative to an in-plane magnetic field, we directly probe the superfluid stiffness via the kinetic inductance. As the field increases, the resonance frequency exhibits a non-monotonic and strongly anisotropic evolution that cannot be explained by orbital pair breaking alone. We show that this behavior is consistent with the emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces, which selectively suppress the supercurrent response depending on the direction of the magnetic field. Microscopic calculations of the stiffness tensor capture the observed anisotropy driven by the interplay of Zeeman and orbital Fulde-Ferrell effects. Our results establish microwave stiffness measurements as a sensitive probe of anisotropic gapless superconductivity in hybrid systems.
item.dc:creator: S. Feyrer, V. Dimic, I. Lobato, A. Kirchner, P. Drexler, L. Rupp, D. Bougeard, T. Lindemann, S. Gronin, G. Gardner, M. J. Manfra, G. F. R. Ruiz, C. A. Balseiro, L. Arrachea, M. Aprili, N. Paradiso, C. Strunk, L. Tosi

item.title: Unconventional Pressure Evolution of Spin-Density-Wave State in La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$
item.description: arXiv:2608.17505v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The discovery of pressure-induced high temperature superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$ has raised the question of how its spin-density-wave (SDW) state evolves toward the superconducting regime. Here, we report a systematic electronic Raman study of La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$ single crystals under hydrostatic pressures up to 16.51~GPa. Both the SDW gap energy and the transition temperature $T_{\mathrm{SDW}}$ show an overall increase with pressure, while the dimensionless coupling ratio $2\Delta_{\mathrm{SDW}}/(k_{\mathrm B}T_{\mathrm{SDW}})$ remains approximately pressure independent, indicating a robust strong-coupling character of SDW state. At the same time, the SDW-related Raman peak broadens as pressure is applied, indicating the enhanced damping of the associated electronic excitation. These results reveal an unusual pressure evolution in which the SDW energy scale is enhanced while the SDW state becomes progressively less coherent, providing spectroscopic constraints on the magnetic correlations relevant to superconductivity in bilayer nickelates.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoxiang Zhou, Shiyu Xie, Liangxin Qiao, Hengyuan Zhang, Jun Shu, Rui Liu, Mengwu Huo, Deyuan Hu, Hengjie Liu, Chuansheng Hu, Ge He, Zeming Qi, Meng Wang, Dong-Lai Feng, Zengyi Du

item.title: Hybridized-Mode Parametric Amplifier in Kinetic-Inductance Circuits
item.description: arXiv:2512.03362v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Parametric amplification is essential for quantum measurement, enabling the amplification of weak microwave signals with minimal added noise. While Josephson-junction-based amplifiers have become standard in superconducting quantum circuits, their magnetic sensitivity, limited saturation power, and sub-kelvin operating requirements motivate the development of alternative nonlinear platforms. Here we demonstrate a two-mode kinetic-inductance parametric amplifier based on a pair of capacitively coupled Kerr-nonlinear resonators fabricated from NbTiN and NbN thin films. The distributed Kerr nonlinearity of these materials enables nondegenerate four-wave-mixing amplification with gains approaching 40 dB, gain-bandwidth products up to 6.9 MHz, and 1-dB compression powers two to three orders of magnitude higher than those of state-of-the-art Josephson amplifiers. A coupled-mode theoretical model accurately captures the pump-induced modification of the hybridized modes and quantitatively reproduces the observed signal and idler responses. The NbN device exhibits a significantly larger Kerr coefficient and superior gain-bandwidth performance, highlighting the advantages of high-kinetic-inductance materials. Our results establish coupled kinetic-inductance resonators as a robust platform for broadband, high-power, and magnetically resilient quantum-limited amplification, offering a scalable route for advanced readout in superconducting qubits, spin ensembles, quantum dots, and other microwave-quantum technologies.
item.dc:creator: Danial Davoudi, Abdul Mohamed, Shabir Barzanjeh

item.title: Experimental realization of a $\cos(2\varphi)$ transmon qubit
item.description: arXiv:2603.13114v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Symmetry-based selection rules make some atomic states remarkably long-lived, a protection superconducting circuits usually lack. We report coherent control and single-shot readout of a 13.6 MHz $\cos 2\varphi$ qubit in the soft-transmon regime. It consists of an island shunted to ground through an interferometer of Josephson junctions and superinductances that favors tunneling of pairs of Cooper pairs, so that Cooper-pair parity symmetry protects the qubit from dielectric loss. We measure a qubit charge matrix element over 100 times smaller than that of the circuit's unprotected plasmon transition, placing the dielectric limit on the qubit lifetime above 10 ms. The measured $T_1 = 70\,\mu$s is instead predicted, with no free parameters, by the $1/f$ flux noise in the interferometer loop that limits dephasing ($T_{2\mathrm{E}} = 2.5\,\mu$s). This experiment demonstrates that Cooper-pair parity symmetry protects against the dielectric loss it targets, and that the remaining limit is the interferometer's sensitivity to flux noise, which larger superinductances are predicted to reduce without compromising protection.
item.dc:creator: Erwan Roverc'h, Alvise Borgognoni, Marius Villiers, Kyrylo Gerashchenko, W. Clarke Smith, Christopher Wilson, Benoit Dou\c{c}ot, Alexandru Petrescu, Philippe Campagne-Ibarcq, Zaki Leghtas

item.title: Fractionalized Fermi liquids with the ghost-Gutzwiller Ansatz
item.description: arXiv:2607.12410v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fractionalized Fermi liquids ($\mathrm{FL}^{\!*}$), elusive metallic states characterized by fractionalized quasiparticles alongside conventional ones and defying Luttinger's theorem, are prime candidates for the pseudogap regime of underdoped cuprates. We show that a $\mathrm{FL}^{\!*}$ phase emerges in the single-band $t$-$J$ model through a simple ghost-Gutzwiller Ansatz, optimized at the cost of a mean-field calculation. The resulting temperature-doping phase diagram encompasses a low-doping $\mathrm{FL}^{\!*}$, a $d$-wave superconducting dome, and an overdoped conventional Fermi liquid, thereby reproducing key qualitative features of cuprate phenomenology.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Pasqua, Carlos Mejuto-Zaera, Michele Fabrizio

item.title: Topologically protected zero-reflection nodes for perfect crossed Andreev reflection
item.description: arXiv:2608.26702v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generating non-locally entangled electron pairs via Cooper-pair splitting is vital for solid-state quantum information processing. However, isolating the underlying crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) is challenging due to competing transport processes like electron tunneling (ET) and local Andreev reflection (AR). Here, we propose a flux-tunable four-terminal normal metal-superconductor junction that achieves deterministic, 100\% efficient CAR. We demonstrate that at exactly half a magnetic flux quantum ($\phi=\pi$), exact destructive Aharonov-Bohm and Peierls interferences structurally forbid ET and AR, respectively. By tuning the central junction hopping, electron reflection is also suppressed to zero. Using the Cauchy argument principle, we prove that this zero-reflection node is topologically protected by a quantized winding number in parameter space. When combined with the precise spatial symmetries of the junction, this exact suppression guarantees a unit CAR probability. We establish that this regime is characterized by a strictly positive cross-correlation shot noise, providing an unambiguous experimental signature of Cooper-pair splitting. Furthermore, this perfect CAR is nearly broadband within the superconducting gap. While generic structural disorder breaks the spatial symmetries required for the exact cancellation of ET and AR, the crossed Andreev reflection--though no longer perfectly quantized --remains highly dominant under weak disorder, offering a resilient architecture for deterministic nonlocal entanglement generation.
item.dc:creator: Abhiram Soori

item.title: Influence of pairing and correlations on transport properties in three-terminal superconducting nanostructure
item.description: arXiv:2610.40059v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the local and nonlocal charge transport properties of three-terminal nanostructure, consisting of the correlated quantum dot embedded between two metallic electrodes and superconductor. Using the linear response theory, we analyze interplay of the induced on-dot pairing with the correlation effects, inspecting their influence on the conductance and thermopower. Our calculations predict negative values of the nonlocal conductance and reversal of the Seebeck coefficient when the quantum dot ground state is represented by the BCS-type singlet configuration. These phenomena are realized when the subgap charge transport is predominantly contributed by the crossed Andreev scattering. In contrast, on the doublet side, we obtain signatures for the Kondo effect manifested by the low-temperature enhancement of the charge conductance and clearly evident in the thermopower. Such temperature-dependent local and nonlocal transport properties can unambiguously identify the specific configuration of the correlated quantum dot and reveal the rich physics emerging in the doublet-to-singlet crossover region.
item.dc:creator: G. G\'orski, V. Pokorn\'y, T. Doma\'nski
